stories.title: Thar women challenge gender stereotypes as global campaign against violence begins
summary: The historic Palan Bazaar, adorned in orange to symbolise hope for a future free from violence against women and girls, became the venue for a dialogue on gender equality, women’s empowerment and the need to dismantle discriminatory social practices.

Speakers at the gathering stressed that discriminatory social norms not only deprived women of educational and employment opportunities but also perpetuated unequal power relations, discouraged survivors of violence from seeking justice and contributed to a culture of impunity.

They called for greater political commitment, effective implementation of laws, institutional accountability and collective efforts to ensure that women and girls could exercise their fundamental rights without fear of violence, discrimination or social exclusion.

stories.title: Student shot in foot as rival groups clash at Sindh University
summary: HYDERABAD: A third-year commerce student received bullet injuries to his foot at Sindh University (SU) on Wednesday during a clash between two groups of students.
The injured student was taken to Liaquat University Hospital.
According to an SU spokesman, the VC has advised students to focus on their studies and said disciplinary action would be taken accordingly.

stories.title: Sindh CM inaugurates Siemens training academy at Karachi's NED University
summary: The academy, established through a partnership between Siemens Pakistan and NED University, is the first of its kind at an engineering university and joins the company’s global network of 29 power academies across 28 countries.

It will provide specialised technical training and certification for customers and industry professionals, while giving students access to practical, industry-relevant learning and Siemens technology during their university education.

Paul Fairweather, MD of the Electrification and Automation Business Unit at Siemens Middle East, said, “What makes Pakistan unique is that we are taking a global Siemens training model into a university for the first time.

stories.title: Sindh High Court restores dissolution of marriage provision in Christian divorce law
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court on Wednesday revived a provision of the Divorce Act of 1869 that had been omitted in 1981, enabling Christian couples in the province to approach courts for dissolution of marriage on ordinary grounds.

Former military dictator Ziaul Haq had omitted Section 7 of the Divorce Act through an ordinance in July 1981, leaving Christian citizens with no ground to divorce their spouses except on charges of adultery.

The bench noted in its judgement that, apparently, the divorce law had recognised cruelty and desertion for two years or more as conduct sufficiently grave to warrant a decree of judicial separation, but not on their own as grounds for dissolution of the marriage.

stories.title: Anthropic chief denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
summary: In February, Amodei told The New York Times that in “life-critical, safety-critical cases, we really want to turn it over” to AI.

Yet in its IPO filing, Anthropic said that “each new version of a Claude model directly accelerates development of the next,” and that Claude wrote over 90 per cent of the contributions to its codebase in September.
Elon Musk, who has long predicted that superintelligent AI would leave humans “like pet Labradors,” reposted Amodei’s statement with a one-word comment: “interesting.”

stories.title: Curtains on COP31
summary: COP31 reaffirmed that multilateralism must endure as the backbone of climate action.

The failure at COP31 should not be viewed as the collapse of the global climate effort but as an urgent signal that the status quo in multilateral climate negotiations is insufficient to meet the scale and immediacy of the crisis.
COP31 may have faltered but it reaffirmed the essential truth that multilateralism must endure as the backbone of climate action.

stories.title: Choking the provinces
summary: In FY2011, the first year after the seventh NFC award, the federal government “successfully pressed” the provincial governments to run a surplus and not spend all the money being devolved down to them.

By June 2015 the IMF programme called for written agreement from the provinces to raise their surpluses, as a prior action and a few months later, in September, provincial spending was capped at 6.5 per cent of GDP.

By June 2016, as the programme was winding up with only a few months left in it, the government set up the Fiscal Coordination Committee to ensure that centre and provinces coordinate their spending and surpluses.

stories.title: Red lines
summary: INTERIOR Minister Mohsin Naqvi is right to say that freedom of expression cannot be a licence to promote terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence or child sexual exploitation.
But assurances count for little while media organisations and journalists are still being intimidated.

A sensible first step would be to bring journalists and their representative bodies, media owners, civil society and relevant state institutions together to agree on what responsible expression means in practice.

stories.title: Govt raises Rs689bn via treasury bills
summary: The three-month bill attracted the highest bids, at Rs902.8bn, against whi­ch the government raised Rs69bn.
Bids for the six-month tenor were the lowest, at Rs483.9bn, with only Rs1bn accepted.
For one-month bills, bids totalled Rs627.5bn, with Rs25bn accepted.

stories.title: Balochistan CM Bugti warns against anti-state narratives
summary: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti said no leniency will be shown to anyone taking up arms against the state or advocating terrorism, regardless of whether they are men or women.
Addressing participants of the 28th National Security Workshop, Mr Bugti outlined the province’s security situation, governance challenges and development priorities.

The chief minister added that the sacrifices made by residents and security forces for peace will not go in vain, reaffirming his government’s commitment to maintaining law and order while addressing public grievances.

stories.title: Lahore High Court seeks police report on Maulana Fazl’s confinement
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Wednesday sought a report from the capital police chief on a petition challenging the alleged confinement of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to his temporary residence in the city.

Judge warns of consequences if JUI-F chief illegally detained Justice Bajwa remarked that if Maulana Fazl had been placed under detention, the authorities would have to provide reasons for the action.
Advocate Hussain said he had been allowed to meet the JUI-F chief after repeatedly requesting the police for permission.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, wife and daughters
summary: The strike that killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the internal security service in northern Gaza, and his family was the second Israeli attack to kill a senior Hamas security official since Tuesday.

The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who “served as a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s (Israeli Defence Forces) counterterrorism operations in the Gaza Strip”.

On Tuesday, after the military killed Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of internal security for all Gaza, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said there was no escape for Hamas from his country’s “long reach”.

stories.title: PTI disowns Achakzai’s call for national govt
summary: Sources revealed that in the meeting it had been decided that no party member would issue any policy statement on the issue of new provinces until the government releases its draft proposal.

According to the sources, the meeting was interrupted for a brief time due to exchange of heated arguments betw­e­en party’s Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and parliamentary leader in the Senate Barrister Ali Zafar.
Mr Khosa reportedly said that Mr Khan had directed him that the issue of new provinces should be discussed in the parliamentary party meeting.

stories.title: Reminiscing about 1990s Karachi, Tajik ambassador pours his heart out
summary: In order to create a diplomatic staff for Tajikistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs the first brotherly country to offer to train us was the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Shares fond memories of a vibrant city at ESUP talk “Pakistan played a crucial role in my life.
Once when we were at an electronic shop, we were speaking among ourselves in the Tajik language though we spoke with the shopkeepers in Urdu.

stories.title: Auqaf dept reviews special initiatives at seven shrines across Punjab
summary: The meeting reviewed arrangements made for visiting Sikh pilgrims from Pakistan and abroad, particularly the United States and Canada, as well as students from educational institutions to various shrines across the province.
The meeting was informed that Sikh pilgrims visited the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir (RA), where they were briefed by the Auqaf Manager, Circle No. 5, about its religious and historical significance.
A delegation of Sikh pilgrims from the United States and Canada also visited the shrine of Hazrat Pir Waris Shah (RA), where Auqaf officials warmly welcomed them and facilitated their visit.

stories.title: Three killed across Punjab in ‘CCD encounters’
summary: Police claimed that Hamza was being taken for recovery by a CCD team when his unidentified accomplices intercepted them along the Noshehra Virkan Road and opened fire.
When the firing stopped, the suspect was found dead by the firing of his own accomplices, who managed to flee the scene, police claimed.
Police claimed that a CCD team confronted suspects riding bikes near the Naimoana Road and firing was exchanged between the team and the outlaws.

stories.title: PM stresses IT potential for economic growth
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday reiterated the government’s commitment to harnessing Pakistan’s IT export potential as a key driver of economic growth and youth employment.

At a review meeting on the information technology and telecommunication sectors, the prime minister directed the formation of a committee to conduct a third-party audit of all operational IT parks under the Special Technology Zones Authority (STZA).

Loss-making SOEs Chairing a separate meeting to review progress on the privatisation of state-owned enterprises and assets, the prime minister directed the relevant authorities to identify additional loss-making SOEs for divestment.

stories.title: New images reveal crater on small asteroid struck by spacecraft in 2022
summary: Dimorphos, an oblong-shaped rocky object about 495 feet (151 metres) wide, orbits its companion asteroid Didymos, with a diameter of 2,395 feet (730 metres), and the pair is currently about 193.5 million km from Earth.
Previous data showed how DART succeeded in changing the path of Dimorphos demonstrating that a spacecraft could alter the trajectory of an object headed toward a collision with Earth.

Hera is now getting a close-up look at how DART physically changed Dimorphos. “The side impacted is now completely covered by a crater, with the visual impression that a piece of the asteroid was cut off by the impact.

stories.title: Gift is not a toll levied at gate of reconciliation: SC
summary: The Supreme Court bench, which also comprised Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan, directed the appellant to pay Rs500,000 in costs to the respondent, Sabiha Iqbal, within 30 days of the judgement.

While rejecting the husband’s claim to the property, Justice Waheed also considered whether the appeal should be dismissed without imposing costs. “Given the circumstances stated above, our answer is no,” the judgement said.

The costs, it observed, were not merely the price of losing a case but also served as a balm for the wounds inflicted by a vexatious litigant. “The respondent has been kept in court for over 28 years over the only home she and her children have.

stories.title: Spanish hunter bags prized Himalayan ibex
summary: GILGIT: A Spanish citizen legally hunted a trophy-size Himalayan ibex in Gilgit-Baltistan region on Tuesday, the same day wildlife officials arrested a suspected poacher in a nearby valley.

Miguel Gorostidi Martinez De Ubago of Spain shot the ibex, which featured 44-inch horns, in a Community Controlled Hunting Area in upper Hunza’s Misgar area, according to wildlife management officer Shabbirullah Baig.

Separately on Tuesday morning, wildlife watchman Shah Jahangir apprehended Haramosh resident Nadir Aman with two illegally hunted Himalayan ibexes during a routine patrol in Gojal Valley’s Khyber village.

stories.title: Ways to boost investment in Gwadar explored
summary: GWADAR: A high-level meeting at the Gwadar Port Authority explored ways to attract Chinese investment and promote industrial activities in the Gwadar Free Zone.

Chaired by GPA Chairman Noorul Haq Baloch, the meeting was attended by China Overseas Port Holding Company Chairman Professor Hu Bo, Guangdong Metal Processing Industry Association Chairperson Ms Yang, Chengdu Company representatives and GPA officials.
Mr Baloch highlighted Gwadar’s strategic location, investment incentives, duty exemptions and direct access to international markets.

stories.title: Glasner demands 'standards and stability' after poor Forest start
summary: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner believes standards at the club were not good enough prior to his arrival as he questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after a number of years in the country.
"For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English." Forest had four different managers during last season as they narrowly avoided relegation just a year after qualifying for Europe.
"We want to create a stable Nottingham Forest team that can consistently play in the top half of the Premier League," Glasner added.

stories.title: Gordon hits double as Barcelona cruise to Sabah victory
summary: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish.

The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League.

"It's always difficult to play a Champions League game, everyone can talk about Barca and our team but if (Sabah) are in the Champions League it means they have good players, so it's not easy at all," Jesus told Movistar.

stories.title: K-P sits on mineral wealth but earns little, says policy paper
summary: According to the provincial government's Budget White Paper 2026-27, non-tax revenue from the mineral sector stood at just Rs10.7 billion in 2024-25.

The policy paper recommended a comprehensive overhaul of the province's mineral governance framework, including the establishment of a Provincial Geological Survey Department and a research consortium involving universities and relevant scientific institutions.

It also called for independent technical and financial audits of existing mining concessions, scientific assessment and certification of mineral reserves, and a review of royalty structures, concession agreements and revenue-sharing arrangements.

stories.title: Sexual violence response unified
summary: A framework has been launched in Punjab for the prevention of sexual violence, protection of victims and access to justice through improved institutional responses and continuous support to victims.
Under the framework, more than 20 government departments have been integrated into a strategy for preventing sexual violence and supporting victims.
A core objective of the framework is to ensure the provision of continuous psychological, medical, legal and financial support to victims of sexual violence.

stories.title: Woman, two children found slaughtered in Sheikhupura
summary: A 23-year-old woman and her two young children were found dead at their home in a village near Sheikhupura after an incident in which the woman allegedly killed the children before taking her own life, police said.
However, the case took another turn after Asifa's father, Amanat Ali, lodged a complaint against members of her in-laws' family at Bhikki Police Station.
He alleged that Asifa had frequently been subjected to quarrels and mistreatment by her husband Shahid, father-in-law Mansha, and two other family members, Mujahid and Farzana.

stories.title: PIA passengers in UK left distressed as 2 flights cancelled due to abrupt Norse Atlantic suspension
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Wednesday it will move its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic Airways abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester.

The development came after Norse Atlantic, a long-haul budget carrier, said its financial situation is “critical” and it requires new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

Norse Atlantic says financial situation ‘critical’ In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: Approved for two floors, built seven - then came the collapse
summary: The tragedy has claimed three lives and left 13 injured, while police have detained five people, including the contractor, and six Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) officials have been suspended.
Meanwhile, Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi has suspended six SBCA officials, including the director of Chanesar Town, relevant deputy directors, assistant directors and building inspectors.
Local resident Faisal Zubair said construction of the building's six floors had been completed on Tuesday, after which work began on a seventh floor intended to house a penthouse.

stories.title: Multimillion-dollar scam: call centre duped Americans
summary: The agency has arrested five suspects in connection with the alleged racket, recovering Rs150 million in cash, cryptocurrency worth approximately Rs60 million and four luxury vehicles.
Investigators believe around Rs1.2 billion in suspected proceeds of the fraud was channelled into Pakistan through illegal hawala and hundi networks and merchant facilities.

The information was then passed on to a US-based medical billing partner, which allegedly used it to file fraudulent claims with American health insurance providers, including Medicare, Humana and UnitedHealthcare.

stories.title: Hyderabad's open manholes become death traps
summary: The Hyderabad Water and Sewerage Corporation (HWSC), which is responsible for sewerage services, has reportedly backed away from installing manhole covers, citing a shortage of funds.

The provincial government restructured the city's municipal administration by establishing nine towns under the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation and replaced the former Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) with the HWSC to improve civic services.
Hyderabad's sewerage network runs largely through underground pipelines, with thousands of manholes spread across the city's three talukas.

stories.title: CT scan machine reduced to a shell
summary: A CT scan machine at Sindh Government Hospital Liaquatabad has remained out of order for nearly a decade, with valuable components allegedly stolen and sold to private hospitals, leaving little more than its outer structure.
According to hospital sources, the CT scan machine became non-functional in 2016, but no effective measures were taken over the years to restore the facility.
Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Aamir Haroon confirmed that the CT scan facility had remained non-operational for years.

stories.title: Below 75% attendance could cost students their exams
summary: Students enrolled in government colleges across Sindh will have to maintain at least 75 per cent attendance to qualify for examinations, with the provincial government announcing strict enforcement of the requirement and ruling out any relaxation for those who fall short.

The conference reviewed the persistent decline in student attendance at government colleges, examined the reasons behind the trend and discussed practical measures to improve classroom participation, strengthen teaching and raise academic standards.
"There will be no compromise on this requirement," he said, stressing that the performance of colleges depended on student enrolment, attendance and administrative discipline.

stories.title: Bangladesh ties of 'great importance' to Pakistan, President and PM tell visiting parliament speaker
summary: Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafizuddin Ahmad on Wednesday met with President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where the Pakistani leaders reaffirmed that Islamabad attached “great importance” to its ties with Dhaka.
The president expressed Islamabad’s desire to further strengthen parliamentary cooperation with Dhaka, as well as highlighted bilateral cooperation in the education and media sectors.

President Zardari welcomed progress under the China-Bangladesh-Pakistan Trilateral Mechanism, particularly the identification of 12 priority areas of cooperation during the Kunming meeting on June 19, 2025, the statement said.

stories.title: Hina case: DNA findings raise fresh questions
summary: The victim's husband and father-in-law have been declared innocent, placed in Column No. 2 of the challan, and their honourable release has been sought.

It has argued that the husband's DNA matching samples from the victim's body, blood and the room latch constitutes significant crime-scene evidence, which the police allegedly continued to conceal deliberately.

The family said it was also awaiting the prosecution branch's decision on the challan and would approach the District and Sessions Judge next week to file the judicial FIR through a private complaint.

stories.title: PIMS medical waste racket busted
summary: Eight suspects have been arrested, while 4,272 kilogrammes of hazardous medical waste have been recovered and destroyed in Lahore.
According to officials, the FIA Islamabad Zone conducted a raid following an investigation into the alleged illegal purchase and sale of medical waste generated by PIMS.
Investigations revealed that a contract for the disposal of PIMS medical waste had been awarded to a company, Chaudhry Noor Zaman and Company.

stories.title: Bajaur mourns as govt mum over Libya boat tragedy
summary: Several families across Bajaur were left shell-shocked and plunged into mourning after reports emerged that 35 local youths had died and several others were missing following a boat accident off the Libyan coast while attempting to reach Europe through illegal routes.
According to local sources, the victims' families said agents who had arranged their journeys abroad had informed them about the accident and the deaths of their loved ones.
In Bajaur, meanwhile, locals said the deaths of 25 young men had so far been confirmed by their families and the agents who had arranged their journeys.

stories.title: Makkah pact trio to meet in Islamabad
summary: Diplomatic sources said the meeting would provide an opportunity to review progress on the institutional framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and discuss ways to strengthen military coordination among the three countries.

At an emergency meeting in Riyadh in October, the three countries agreed to move towards implementing their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan subsequently said Ankara and Islamabad were assessing possible support for Saudi Arabia in areas such as air defence, electronic warfare and technical assistance.
